A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CopulaLSP research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original prediction, runtime, memory, ablation, and sensitivity results in Section 5, plus correlation-modeling and synthetic-graph experiments in Appendices B and F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the real-world benchmark comparisons and synthetic-graph experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the relaxed Bernoulli marginals, Gramian correlation construction, label-smoothed likelihood objective, and Woodbury inference. Describing SNEA as the implemented signed-graph encoder clarifies the existing architecture without changing it.

E1.justification: Both evaluate link sign prediction on BitcoinAlpha, BitcoinOTC, WikiElec, WikiRfa, SlashDot, and Epinions. Appendix F.2 retains the same 40-node synthetic graph with two symmetric communities; no dataset or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons retain GCN, SGCN, SNEA, SDGNN, TrustSGCN, SLGNN, SGAAE, and SE-SGformer. The synthetic experiment still compares against SNEA. Newly cited recommendation methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain AUC and macro F1, the 8:1:1 real-data split, fixed Gaussian node features, the same preprocessing, and standardized logistic regression for embedding-based methods. Appendix F.2 also retains its 8:2 split and 10-epoch synthetic experiment.

E4.justification: The identity-versus-Gramian and Woodbury ablations, sensitivity studies for label smoothing, epsilon, and embedding size, Appendix B correlation-capacity experiment, and Appendix F.2 component visualizations are all retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix F continue to report averages over 10 distinct data splits. There are no changes to run-count disclosures, uncertainty reporting, or statistical testing practices.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, rankings, and appendix outcomes are retained. Table 5 rounds the BitcoinAlpha and BitcoinOTC inference speedups from 3.7× and 8.8× to 4× and 9×; the corresponding timings are unchanged, so this is equivalent rounding rather than a result change.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Woodbury derivation, and convergence proofs remain unchanged. Appendix A replaces f with f_simple at the end of the CDF derivative calculation; these denote algebraically equivalent densities already given in v1, so no mathematical reasoning changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: scalable inter-edge correlation modeling, efficient Woodbury inference, linear convergence, and competitive prediction performance with faster computation.

C2.justification: The explanations of convergence, memory tradeoffs, hyperparameter behavior, and synthetic-graph mechanisms are retained. The static-graph limitation and proposed extensions to dynamic and bipartite graphs are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains PyTorch 2.7, CUDA 12.4, A6000 hardware and A5000 ablation hardware, preprocessing instructions, evaluation details, and best hyperparameters. No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The introduction adds citations to Content-based graph reconstruction for cold-start item recommendation and ReducedGCN. The general 1991 copula-volume citation is replaced by Schweizer's chapter, Thirty years of copulas. These are limited reference changes; the positioning relative to CopulaGNN and signed GNNs remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 makes local wording and notation edits, clarifies the encoder description, shortens the affiliation block, expands acknowledgments, and revises bibliographic metadata, including GCN author attribution. Sections and narrative organization remain intact. Section 5.1 introduces the grammatical slip 'results are provides'.

P2.justification: The shortened front matter and revised references cause local reflow, including moving Equation (4) from page 3 to page 2. Some table sizing and spacing also change slightly. All figures and tables retain their identities, content structure, and captions; none is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves attribution and clarity through fuller GCN authorship, a specific copula-chapter reference replacing the malformed volume entry, and clearer encoder wording and notation. The scientific evidence and proofs remain unchanged. A new grammatical slip in Section 5.1 slightly offsets these editorial gains, so the overall improvement is limited.
